questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full semitrailers attached.

options.text: Quicker
Easier
More difficult

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no semitrailer attached. When driving a bobtail, stopping is harder and takes a longer distance than when a tractor is pulling a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle turns a corner:

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels will move in different paths.
It is best to let the rear wheels drive over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels will move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Vehicles with trailers show this effect more.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: Regularly to activate the trailer brakes in all driving conditions.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid.
Only if the trailer is carrying a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the trailer brakes. Do not use it while driving because it may cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: Look into the back of the fifth wheel:

options.text: While testing your air brakes.
If your vehicle begins to skid.
When inspecting a coupling.

questions.correctAnswerText: When inspecting a coupling.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: In a combination rig, it is best to make:

options.text: Quick, sudden stops.
Sharp turns.
Quick accelerations.
Slow, planned stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow, planned stops.
questions.explanation: When driving a combination vehicle, brake well in advance and look ahead to avoid sudden stops. These habits help prevent your trailer from jackknifing.

questions.question: The "crack-the-whip" effect can:

options.text: Turn over a trailer.
Be more effective than braking.
Make a truck move faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn over a trailer.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause trailers to tip over. The last trailer in a combination is most likely to tip. Know your vehicle's rearward amplification and drive safely.

questions.question: If you are backing and become unsure about your path, you should:

options.text: Continue backing.
Stop and get out to look.
Continue backing, but more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure of your path while backing, stop the vehicle, get out, and check your path of travel.

questions.question: One way to prevent a rollover is to:

options.text: Move cargo to the left side of the rig.
Keep cargo centered on the rig.
Move cargo to the right side of the rig.
Keep cargo as far from the ground as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo centered on the rig.
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading increases rollover risk. Keep your load centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: When coupling, you should:

options.text: Make sure to couple the correct glad hands.
Only couple one set of glad hands.
Leave one glad hand loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple the correct glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect the correct pairs of glad hands when coupling air brake hoses. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is typically for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: When the wheels of a trailer lock up:

options.text: The trailer will be drivable.
The trailer may swing around.
The vehicle will maintain steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is especially likely with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: The easiest way to know your trailer is skidding is to:

options.text: Ask another driver.
Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left its lane.
Release the brake pedal and press it again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left its lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is still in the right position.

questions.question: When driving a tractor-trailer with ABS, you should:

options.text: Brake harder than normal.
Use extra braking force to make ABS activate.
Brake the same way you normally do.
Use less braking pressure than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you normally do.
questions.explanation: Brake a tractor-trailer with ABS the same way you would brake a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: Test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Removing the air supply knob.
Removing the parking brake control knob.
Releasing air with the brake pedal.
Releasing air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully. Turn off the engine. Then press the brake pedal several times to release air from the system. The tractor protection valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels:

options.text: Follow the same path as the front wheels.
Follow a different path than the front wheels.
Should not be a concern to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning a corner. This is called off-tracking. Longer vehicles have more off-tracking than shorter vehicles.

questions.question: A trolley valve:

options.text: Should be used while driving.
Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
Should be used when parking uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (trolley valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Never use it while parking because it may release air pressure and release the brakes that hold the vehicle in place.

questions.question: To find out if a vehicle built before 1998 has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you can:

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Look for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: If you drive a vehicle built before 1998 and are not sure if it has ABS, look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer:

options.text: May lean and could roll over.
May have extra support during turns.
May have improved braking.
May have improved steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: May lean and could roll over.
questions.explanation: If the load weight is mostly on one side of the trailer, the trailer may lean to one side. This increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer has started to skid is by:

options.text: Seeing other drivers' faces.
Checking the trailer in your mirrors.
Feeling the trailer move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors to spot a trailer skid or jackknife. This lets you catch any skidding as early as possible.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:

options.text: Supply air to the trailer.
Block the wheels.
Inspect the fifth wheel.
Connect the electrical cord.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer. Following the correct coupling steps is important for safely operating a combination vehicle.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downgrade.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while parking because it may release air pressure and release the brakes that hold the vehicle in place. Instead, use the parking brake or wheel chocks.
